result.topic_en: Reprinted unsolved questions: the end of a question by G. Fontené on division with a remainder of smaller norm, Fontené's question 2151 on a determinant related to the Euler-Maclaurin formula, R. Gilbert's question 2156 on a recursively defined sequence of polynomials, and the beginning of question 2161 on a regular pyramid with a rectangular base.

2151 (1910, 239). — Établir directement (pour $n \neq 1$) l'égalité
$\begin{vmatrix} \frac{1}{1.2} & \frac{1}{1} & 0 & 0 & \dots & \dots \\ \frac{1}{1.2.3} & \frac{1}{1.2} & \frac{1}{1} & 0 & \dots & \dots \\ \dots & \dots & . & . & \dots & \dots \\ \frac{1}{(2n)!} & \frac{1}{(2n-1)!} & . & . & \dots & \frac{1}{1.2} \end{vmatrix} = 0$,
relative à la formule de sommation d'Euler-Maclaurin.
G. FONTENÉ.

2156 (1910, 335). — On considère la suite des polynomes en $x$
$P_0,\ P_1,\ P_2,\ P_3,\ \dots,\ P_n,\ \dots$
tels que
$nP_n = (3n-2)P_{n-1} - (3n-4+x^2)P_{n-2}$
$+ (1-x^3)(n-2)P_{n-3}$
avec
$P_0 = P_1 = 1,$
$P_2 = 1 - \frac{x^2}{2},$
. . . . . . . . . . . . .

1° Montrer que l'on a
$P_n = a_0 + C_n^1 a_1 x + C_n^2 a_2 x^2 + \dots + C_n^p a_p x^p + \dots + C_n^n a_n x^n,$
$C_n^p$ étant le nombre des combinaisons de $n$ lettres $p$ à $p$ et $a_p$ étant fonction de $p$ seul indépendant de $x$ et $n$;
2° Montrer qu'il y a une relation linéaire entre $a_p$, $a_{p-1}$, $a_{p-2}$ vérifiée quel que soit $p$. En conclure la valeur de $a_p$ en fonction de $p$.
R. GILBERT.

questions.statement_en:
Establish directly (for $n \neq 1$) the equality
$\begin{vmatrix} \frac{1}{1.2} & \frac{1}{1} & 0 & 0 & \dots & \dots \\ \frac{1}{1.2.3} & \frac{1}{1.2} & \frac{1}{1} & 0 & \dots & \dots \\ \dots & \dots & . & . & \dots & \dots \\ \frac{1}{(2n)!} & \frac{1}{(2n-1)!} & . & . & \dots & \frac{1}{1.2} \end{vmatrix} = 0$,
which relates to the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula.

questions.statement_en:
Consider the sequence of polynomials in $x$
$P_0,\ P_1,\ P_2,\ P_3,\ \dots,\ P_n,\ \dots$
such that
$nP_n = (3n-2)P_{n-1} - (3n-4+x^2)P_{n-2} + (1-x^3)(n-2)P_{n-3}$
with
$P_0 = P_1 = 1,$
$P_2 = 1 - \frac{x^2}{2},$
. . .
1° Show that
$P_n = a_0 + C_n^1 a_1 x + C_n^2 a_2 x^2 + \dots + C_n^p a_p x^p + \dots + C_n^n a_n x^n,$
where $C_n^p$ is the number of combinations of $n$ letters taken $p$ at a time and $a_p$ is a function of $p$ alone, independent of $x$ and $n$;
2° Show that there is a linear relation among $a_p$, $a_{p-1}$, $a_{p-2}$ that holds for every $p$. Deduce from it the value of $a_p$ as a function of $p$.
